metadata.content: Coco Gauff reports online racial abuse after incident during her victory over Sun Xinran at China Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Coco Gauff reports online racial abuse after incident during her victory over Sun Xinran at China Open Coco Gauff has had to endure online racial abuse after her latest victory at the China Open; The American star beat 16-year-old Sun Xinran in straight sets though there was an incident at a key moment when Gauff had to stop a point; Gauff explained the "unfortunate situation" Monday 5 October 2026 22:11, UK Image: Coco Gauff has progressed at the China Open (Associated Press) Coco Gauff has said she has been racially abused on social media following an incident in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open. The world No 4 won 7-5 6-1 against the 16-year-old from China to progress to the last 16 in Beijing. Gauff was serving to stay in the first set at 4-5 when Sun thought she had hit a winner, but the American had already raised her hand to stop the point as a light in the side panels around the court was flickering. Gauff took the next three points to hold for 5-5, and then dropped just one more game in the match. The 22-year-old tried to explain the situation on X, saying: "It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control. Eventually, this collaboration of lateral thinking which ensured a Grand Prix took place on a great track we have missed in F1 for nine years, was a huge success. I want to say straight away that I know from meeting numerous fans over the weekend, particularly at the airport on Monday morning, that a great many people suffered very long delays getting out of the venue and back to their bases. Road systems became gridlocked and transit buses blocked. While the event was necessarily hurriedly assembled, this was still disappointing, and I want to add my personal appreciation to those fans in Malaysia. metadata.content: Ben Whittaker: Conor Wallace scare raises questions over light-heavyweight's title credentials, says Matthew Macklin | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Ben Whittaker: Conor Wallace scare raises questions over light-heavyweight's title credentials, says Matthew Macklin Ben Whittaker beat Conor Wallace by unanimous decision in Birmingham on Saturday, despite a wobbly final three rounds for the Olympic silver medallist; Sky Sports' Matthew Macklin says Whittaker needs more fights before his shot at the IBF light-heavyweight belt which the win earned him Matthew Macklin Boxing Expert and Pundit Monday 5 October 2026 15:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Whittaker survived a final-round fright to beat Conor Wallace on points in Birmingham. Pictures courtesy of DAZN Boxing. Ben Whittaker's recent scare against Conor Wallace has raised questions about whether he has the attributes needed to win a world title, says Sky Sports expert Matthew Macklin. After controlling the fight from the start, Whittaker was troubled by a left hand from Wallace in the 10th round and then looked ragged in the 12th as he repeatedly slipped to the canvas before clinging on to claim a points win on Saturday in Birmingham. Whittaker's victory lined up a shot at the IBF light-heavyweight belt which is held by unified champion Dmitry Bivol, but Macklin believes the Olympic silver medallist is not yet ready to challenge the Russian. metadata.summary: JJ Gabriel is still expected to leave Manchester United despite featuring in the club's squad photo for the 2026/27 season.
metadata.content: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd prodigy still expected to leave despite first-team photo inclusion - this is how it unfolded | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Transfer JJ Gabriel: Man Utd prodigy still expected to leave despite first-team photo inclusion - this is how it unfolded Teenager JJ Gabriel remains registered to Man Utd after his camp put in a formal request to leave, but Sky Sports News reporter Danyal Khan explains why there is very little chance of him staying amid interest from a host of Europe's top clubs and what took place to reach this point... Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Monday 5 October 2026 19:03, UK Image: JJ Gabriel and his camp formally requested to leave Man Utd JJ Gabriel is still expected to leave Manchester United despite featuring in the club's squad photo for the 2026/27 season. Sky Sports News understands the picture was taken on September 8, when Gabriel was still at the club and expected to feature for the first team this season. It was just days later that Gabriel and his family then put in a formal request to leave. Gabriel remains registered with United and Sky Sports News understands multiple attempts have been made to reconcile the situation with the 15-year-old and his family, with duty of care being a factor for such a young player, but no progress has been made.
